references.text: The description of the bronze basin and its stand, which were to be used by the priests for washing. This is the original command to make the basin that is now to be anointed.
The list of items to be anointed with the holy anointing oil, including the bronze basin and its stand.
The description of how the bronze basin and its stand were made from bronze mirrors donated by the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Moses performs the anointing of the tabernacle and all its furnishings, including the basin, to consecrate them.
The command that Aaron and his sons must wash with water, illustrating the purpose of the bronze basin.
The fulfillment of the command where Moses sets up the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, filling it with water for washing.
Complementary instructions in the consecration ceremony: 30:26 covers the tent and ark, while 40:11 specifies the basin.
Theological parallel: Anointing as a necessary means to consecrate cultic objects (the altar in 29:36, the basin in 40:11).
Direct narrative connection: 30:18 describes the making of the basin that is anointed in 40:11.
Theological principle connection: 30:29 explains the consequence (most holy) of the anointing performed in 40:11.
